about: The synthetic cleanup evaluation set. Fixtures/cleanup/README.md defines every field.

cases.title: A negation behind fillers
cases.raw: um so I don't think we should sign the lease yet uh not until the landlord fixes the heating
cases.reference: So I don't think we should sign the lease yet, not until the landlord fixes the heating.
keep: not until the landlord fixes the heating

wrong.output: So I think we should sign the lease yet, not until the landlord fixes the heating.

cases.notes: Both negations stay. The fillers go. "So" is kept: it is not on the filler list.

cases.title: A negation inside a restart
cases.raw: it's not it's not the blue folder it's the green one
cases.reference: It's not the blue folder, it's the green one.
cases.notes: The repeated "it's not" may go because the same negation survives straight after it. Removing both copies of "not" changes the meaning.

cases.title: A split negation in a reminder
cases.raw: remind me to not reply to the email from the bank until I've called them
cases.reference: Remind me to not reply to the email from the bank until I've called them.

wrong.output: Remind me to reply to the email from the bank until I've called them.
wrong.why: Dropping "not" turns a warning into an instruction.

cases.notes: Nothing to remove. Moving "not" to read "not to reply" reorders words, which v1 does not allow.

cases.title: An amount in dollars and cents
cases.raw: pay the plumber 240 dollars um and 50 cents for the parts
cases.reference: Pay the plumber 240 dollars and 50 cents for the parts.

wrong.output: Pay the plumber $240.50 for the parts.
wrong.why: Numbers stay as transcribed in v1. Rewriting the amount is a change of words.

cases.notes: The amount stays exactly as transcribed, digits and words alike.

cases.title: Numbers spoken as words
cases.raw: we need forty two chairs and uh six tables for the hall
cases.reference: We need forty two chairs and six tables for the hall.

wrong.output: We need 42 chairs and 6 tables for the hall.
wrong.why: Converting words to digits changes the words, which v1 does not allow.

cases.notes: Hyphenating "forty-two" is allowed: it is punctuation and keeps both words.

cases.title: A date and a time
cases.raw: the dentist moved my appointment to the 14th of March at 9:30
cases.reference: The dentist moved my appointment to the 14th of March at 9:30.
cases.notes: Capitalising March is a change of case and is allowed. The date and the time stay as written.

cases.title: A date with a negated alternative
cases.raw: the flight is next Friday the 3rd not Thursday
cases.reference: The flight is next Friday the 3rd, not Thursday.

wrong.output: The flight is next Friday the 3rd.
wrong.why: Dropping "not Thursday" loses the warning against the other day.

cases.notes: A full stop before "Not Thursday" is also correct: a sentence break alone does not change the meaning here.

cases.title: Two names, kept as transcribed
cases.raw: send the draft to Siobhan and copy uh Mateus on it
cases.reference: Send the draft to Siobhan and copy Mateus on it.

wrong.output: Send the draft to Siobhan and copy Matthews on it.

cases.notes: Names keep the transcriber's spelling, even when another spelling looks likelier.

cases.title: A title, a name and a date
cases.raw: ask Dr Okafor whether Lena can start on the 2nd
cases.reference: Ask Dr. Okafor whether Lena can start on the 2nd.
cases.notes: Adding the full stop after "Dr" is punctuation and is allowed.

cases.title: A spoken self-correction of a day
cases.raw: let's meet at the café on Tuesday no Wednesday at 10
cases.reference: Let's meet at the café on Tuesday, no, Wednesday at 10.

wrong.output: Let's meet at the café on Wednesday at 10.
wrong.why: v1 leaves a spoken self-correction as it was said. Resolving it is a later feature.

cases.notes: The correction stays word for word. Commas around "no" make it readable.

cases.title: A self-correction of a quantity
cases.raw: buy 2 no 3 bags of rice
cases.reference: Buy 2, no, 3 bags of rice.

wrong.why: The correction is resolved, and a number is dropped.

cases.notes: Both numbers and the "no" between them stay.

cases.title: A self-correction of a code
cases.raw: the door code is 4 7 1 9 sorry 4 7 9 1
cases.reference: The door code is 4 7 1 9, sorry, 4 7 9 1.

wrong.why: Joining the digits rewrites them, and the first code is gone.

cases.notes: "Sorry" is not a filler here: it marks the correction.

cases.title: Punctuation only: "no more than"
cases.raw: no more than five people can come to the tasting
cases.reference: No more than five people can come to the tasting.

wrong.output: No. More than five people can come to the tasting.
wrong.why: Every word is kept, but a limit becomes its opposite.

cases.notes: The guard accepts the wrong output, because the words are the same. Only this check catches it.

cases.title: Punctuation only: how many people
cases.raw: invite Anna Maria and Joe to the dinner
cases.reference: Invite Anna Maria and Joe to the dinner.

wrong.output: Invite Anna, Maria and Joe to the dinner.
wrong.why: A comma turns two guests into three.

cases.notes: The raw text is ambiguous. A correct cleanup does not decide it by adding a comma.

cases.title: Punctuation only: a time and a count
cases.raw: meet at ten thirty two people from finance are joining
cases.reference: Meet at ten thirty. Two people from finance are joining.

wrong.output: Meet at ten. Thirty two people from finance are joining.
wrong.why: The time changes, and so does the number of people.

cases.notes: The reading "ten thirty" is the natural one. A break between "ten" and "thirty" changes both facts.

cases.title: Punctuation only: "not sure"
cases.raw: I'm not sure we should cancel the booking
cases.reference: I'm not sure we should cancel the booking.

wrong.output: I'm not. Sure, we should cancel the booking.
wrong.why: Doubt becomes a decision to cancel.

cases.notes: Nothing to remove and nothing to split.

cases.title: A sentence thick with fillers
cases.raw: um so uh I want to uh like try the new running route tomorrow morning you know the one by the river
cases.reference: So I want to try the new running route tomorrow morning, the one by the river.
keep: try the new running route tomorrow morning
cases.notes: "Like" and "you know" are fillers here. Compare c29 and c30, where they are not.

cases.title: Repeated words
cases.raw: the the meeting with the the design team went well
cases.reference: The meeting with the design team went well.
cases.notes: Each doubled "the" loses one copy.

cases.title: A restart with the same words
cases.raw: we should we should book the hotel this week
cases.reference: We should book the hotel this week.
keep: we should book the hotel this week
cases.notes: The first "we should" repeats the words that follow it, so it goes.

cases.title: A spoken shopping list
cases.raw: shopping list eggs milk bread two lemons and coffee
cases.reference: Shopping list: eggs, milk, bread, two lemons and coffee.
cases.notes: A bulleted list is also correct if it keeps every word, "and" included. Dropping "and" to tidy the list is a removal v1 does not allow.

cases.title: A numbered list said in words
cases.raw: three things for the trip first the passport second the charger third the blue jacket
cases.reference: Three things for the trip: first, the passport; second, the charger; third, the blue jacket.
cases.notes: A numbered list is also correct if "first", "second" and "third" stay.

cases.title: Two topics, two paragraphs
cases.raw: okay two things about the garden the tomato plants need staking before the weekend and the hose by the shed is leaking um separate thing the neighbours asked if they can borrow the ladder on Sunday
cases.reference:
Okay, two things about the garden. The tomato plants need staking before the weekend, and the hose by the shed is leaking.

Separate thing: the neighbours asked if they can borrow the ladder on Sunday.
keep: the tomato plants need staking before the weekend
the hose by the shed is leaking
cases.notes: A paragraph break before "separate thing" is the structure a good cleanup adds.

cases.title: A question
cases.raw: do we still have the spare key for the bike lock or did it go with the old bike
cases.reference: Do we still have the spare key for the bike lock, or did it go with the old bike?
keep: spare key for the bike lock
or did it go with the old bike
cases.notes: It ends with a question mark.

cases.title: Already clean
cases.raw: water the plants
cases.reference: Water the plants.
cases.notes: Only a capital and a full stop are added.

cases.title: Nothing but a filler
cases.raw: um
cases.reference: Um.
cases.notes: Removing the only word would empty the segment. The guard rejects a result that drops more than its set share of the words, and the raw transcript stays.

cases.title: A run-on note
cases.raw: so this morning I went to the market and then I got the bread and then I saw that the fish stall had moved to the other end and uh then I ran into the neighbours and they said the street party is on the last Saturday of the month and we should bring chairs
cases.reference: So this morning I went to the market, and then I got the bread. And then I saw that the fish stall had moved to the other end, and then I ran into the neighbours, and they said the street party is on the last Saturday of the month, and we should bring chairs.
keep: the fish stall had moved to the other end
the last Saturday of the month
cases.notes: Sentences are formed by punctuation alone. The "and then" chains stay: "and" is not a filler, so v1 may not remove it to tidy the sentences.

cases.title: A restart that changes a verb
cases.raw: can you pick up can you grab the parcel from the post office
cases.reference: Can you grab the parcel from the post office?
keep: can you grab the parcel from the post office
cases.notes: A restart: the speaker began again with the same first word, so the abandoned start may go. Keeping it is also correct, as the words are kept.

cases.title: Product names and casing
cases.raw: remind me to update the iOS app and check the API keys tonight
cases.reference: Remind me to update the iOS app and check the API keys tonight.
cases.notes: Casing that the transcriber got right stays.

cases.title: "Like" as a verb and as a filler
cases.raw: I'd like to like book a table for 4 on Saturday
cases.reference: I'd like to book a table for 4 on Saturday.
cases.notes: Only the second "like" is a filler. Removing the first breaks the sentence.

cases.title: "You know" that is not a filler
cases.raw: you know the answer better than I do so just decide
cases.reference: You know the answer better than I do, so just decide.

wrong.output: The answer better than I do, so just decide.
wrong.why: "You know" is the subject and verb here. A filler list that holds "you know" must not apply to it.

cases.notes: The guard's closed filler list allows removing "you know", so the guard alone would accept the wrong output.
